newsitem.title: USA: U.S. stocks seen heading higher at open.
newsitem.headline: U.S. stocks seen heading higher at open.

text.p: Wall Street stocks are expected to open higher, with many investors focusing on General Motors Corp's announcement that it will sell its Hughes Aircraft unit to Raytheon Co.
But they said it was not certain that GM's stock would rally strongly on the news.
"This deal highlights General Motors's non-auto businesses and it is favorable for the company," said Larry Wachtel, analyst at Prudential Securities.

"I don't think people are aware of GM's non-auto assets and this underscores a theme we have for GM in 1997," Wachtel said. "The company's financial shape will get stronger and stronger. We envisage a dividend boost and a share buyback this year."
But he said the Raytheon deal was not a surprise.
"This development has been spaculated about for some time. To say that people will rush in and buy shares of General Motors today is a bit premature," he said.
Wachtel said that today was likely to see some volatility amid double-witching expirations.
In Tokyo the Nikkei Average was down 54 points at 18,090.
In London the FTSE 100 Index was up two points to 4200.
Among U.S. shares traded in London, GM was up 3/8 at 60-3/4.
Eastman Kodak Co was up 3/8 at 85-7/8 following a 4-1/4 jump in New York on news that the company had raised its quarterly dividend and intended to improve its cost structure.
Archer Daniels Midland Co was down 1/4 at 21-5/8. Intel Corp was up 1/2 at 142-7/8, Digital Equipment Corp was up 3/8 at 37-1/4, and International Business Machines Corp was up 1/4 at 165-3/8.
The dollar was off its highs in Tokyo and was testing fresh highs in Europe.
U.S. Treasuries were mostly higher, with the long bond up 6/32 to yield 6.82 percent.
The Wall Street Journal's Heard on the Street column says Barclay's Global Investors is the No. 2 U.S. money manager ranked by assets, building its status via index mutual funds.
The New York Times's Market Place column focuses on the GM-Raytheon deal.
